name: Analytical balance
summary: A 0.1 mg balance with a serial print key. Analysts weigh controlled substances by difference and copy each weight by hand.
today: Analyst copies two weights onto a paper log.
Analyst types the result into the LIMS.
The CS ledger is updated by hand later.
bridged: The tap reads each stable print on the port.
The bridge works out the amount used.
One reading goes to the LIMS and the CS ledger.
connection: Rear panel, the port marked RS-232
A serial printer or a PC reads the port
One line for each press of the print key
S S 25.4790 g: S is stable and D is moving, then the value and the unit

name: HPLC system
summary: A liquid chromatograph run by a legacy chromatography data system. The system prints a peak report. Analysts copy each purity result by hand.
today: The analyst prints the peak report on paper.
The analyst types the purity result into the LIMS.
A software or Windows update can break the old instrument driver.
bridged: The tap reads the peak report that the system prints over the network.
The bridge drops the solvent front and works out purity.
One result goes to the LIMS with its sample and instrument.
specs: Peak report to a network printer
connection: The network cable between the data system and its printer
The chromatography data system prints the peak report to a network printer
One report for each sample run
A text peak table with one row for each peak
No change. The printer stays in the line

name: pH meter
summary: A benchtop pH meter with a serial print port. Analysts wait for the value to settle, then copy the pH by hand.
today: Analyst waits for the display to settle.
Analyst writes the pH and the temperature on a paper log.
Analyst types the pH into the LIMS later.
bridged: The tap reads each line that the meter prints on the port.
The bridge drops the lines that still drift and keeps the last settled value.
One pH result goes to the LIMS with its sample and instrument.
connection: Rear panel, the port marked RS-232
A serial printer or a PC reads the port
One line each second while the meter reads
pH 7.02 25.1C READY: the pH, the temperature, then READY for a settled value or DRIFT for a moving one
